theory.intro: An object moving with **constant velocity** $\underset{\sim}{v}$ travels in a straight line at a steady speed. Its position after time $t$ is $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\underset{\sim}{r}_{0}+t\underset{\sim}{v}$, where $\underset{\sim}{r}_{0}$ is its position at $t=0$.
facts: The **initial position** $\underset{\sim}{r}_{0}$ is where the object is when $t=0$.
Two known positions give the velocity: $\underset{\sim}{v}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{2})-\underset{\sim}{r}(t_{1})}{t_{2}-t_{1}}$.
The **speed** is the magnitude $|\underset{\sim}{v}|$, which is a number, while the velocity is a vector.
Two objects **collide** only if they are at the same position at the same value of $t$.
Paths that cross need not give a collision, because the objects may pass the crossing point at different times.
steps: Write down the initial position and the velocity
Work with the components separately to answer the question

foundation.question_text:
A particle has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}+t\begin{pmatrix}4\\5\end{pmatrix}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Find its position vector when $t=3$.

A drone has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(7-2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(1+3t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Find its position vector when $t=4$.

At $t=0$ a robot is at the point with position vector $-5\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres.
It then moves with constant velocity $3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$ m/s.
Write its position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

A boat starts at the point with position vector $\begin{pmatrix}8\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ km and travels with constant velocity $\begin{pmatrix}-2\\6\end{pmatrix}$ km/h.
Write its position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ as a single column, where $t$ is in hours.

A particle moves with constant velocity.
At $t=1$ s it is at the point $(2,5)$ and at $t=4$ s it is at the point $(14,-1)$, with distances in metres.
Find its velocity vector.

A yacht moves with constant velocity.
At $t=2$ h it is at the point $(-3,4)$ and at $t=6$ h it is at the point $(9,0)$, with distances in kilometres.
Find its velocity vector.

A particle has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(1+6t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4+8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
How fast is the particle moving?

development.question_text:
A particle has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(2+5t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9-3t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
At what time is the particle at the point $(22,-3)$?
development.solution_text:
$2+5t=22$
$5t=20$
$t=4$
Checking the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component:
$9-3\times 4$
$=-3$
The particle is at $(22,-3)$ when $t=4$ s.

development.question_text:
A particle has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(-8+2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(5-t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Find the time at which the particle crosses the $y$-axis, and its position then.
development.solution_text:
On the $y$-axis the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component is zero.
$-8+2t=0$
$2t=8$
$t=4$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(4)$
$=0\underset{\sim}{i}+(5-4)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=\underset{\sim}{j}$
The particle crosses the $y$-axis at $t=4$ s, at the point $(0,1)$.

development.question_text:
Two hikers have positions $\underset{\sim}{r}_{A}(t)=(1+3t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2+t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}_{B}(t)=(9-t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(6+4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ kilometres, where $t$ is in hours.
How far apart are they when $t=2$?

Two particles have positions $\underset{\sim}{r}_{P}(t)=(2+4t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(-1+2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}_{Q}(t)=(10-2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(5-t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Find the exact distance between them when $t=1$.

Two drones have positions $\underset{\sim}{r}_{A}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}+t\begin{pmatrix}3\\5\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}_{B}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}23\\34\end{pmatrix}+t\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-6\end{pmatrix}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Show that the drones collide, and state where and when.
development.solution_text:
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components:
$2+3t=23-4t$
$7t=21$
$t=3$
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components:
$1+5t=34-6t$
$11t=33$
$t=3$
Both components agree at $t=3$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}_{A}(3)=\begin{pmatrix}11\\16\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}_{B}(3)=\begin{pmatrix}11\\16\end{pmatrix}$
The drones collide at the point $(11,16)$ when $t=3$ s.

development.question_text:
Two particles have positions $\underset{\sim}{r}_{A}(t)=2t\underset{\sim}{i}+(1+t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}_{B}(t)=(10-t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(9-2t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
Do the particles collide?
Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components:
$2t=10-t$
$3t=10$
$t=\frac{10}{3}$
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components:
$1+t=9-2t$
$3t=8$
$t=\frac{8}{3}$
The two times are different, so there is no value of $t$ giving the same position for both particles.
The particles do not collide. Their paths do cross at $(8,5)$, but $A$ is there at $t=4$ s and $B$ is there at $t=2$ s.

mastery.question_text:
A particle $P$ has position $\underset{\sim}{r}_{P}(t)=(4+t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(-6+4t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds.
A particle $Q$ starts at the point $(34,36)$ at $t=0$ and moves with constant velocity so that it collides with $P$ when $t=6$.
Find the velocity of $Q$ and its speed.

A particle moves with constant velocity.
At $t=2$ s it is at the point $(5,-4)$ and at $t=7$ s it is at the point $(-5,11)$, with distances in metres.
Find its position at $t=0$ and its exact speed.

Particle $A$ has position $\underset{\sim}{r}_{A}(t)=(1+2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(-3+3t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ and particle $B$ has position $\underset{\sim}{r}_{B}(t)=(13-ct)\underset{\sim}{i}+(21-5t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, where $t$ is in seconds and $c$ is a constant.
Find the value of $c$ for which the particles collide.
mastery.solution_text:
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ components:
$-3+3t=21-5t$
$8t=24$
$t=3$
Equating the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ components at $t=3$:
$1+2\times 3=13-3c$
$7=13-3c$
$3c=6$
$c=2$
At $t=3$ both particles are at $(7,6)$, so $c=2$.
